hints: Focus on what type of reaction each reagent causes, addition across the double bond or oxidative cleavage of it.
Remember that HBr adds to an unsymmetrical alkene by Markovnikov's rule, with Br going to the more substituted carbon.
Compare mild oxidation which keeps the carbon skeleton intact with vigorous oxidation which breaks the C=C bond completely.
walkthrough:
**Start with propene structure**

Propene is an unsymmetrical alkene, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$. Addition reactions break the pi bond and add atoms to the two C atoms, while oxidation with $\text{KMnO}_4$ behaves very differently in cold dilute vs hot concentrated conditions.

**Check the addition reactions**

With $\text{HBr(g)}$, electrophilic addition follows Markovnikov's rule. H adds to the carbon with more H atoms already, Br adds to the more stable carbocation:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 + \text{HBr} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CHBrCH}_3$$
That product is 2-bromopropane. With $\text{Br}_2\text{(aq)}$, bromine water, you do not get simple addition to give a bromoalkane, you get a bromohydrin, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{Br}$.

**Check the two oxidation conditions**

Cold, dilute, acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ gives mild syn-hydroxylation to a diol, propane-1,2-diol:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 + [\text{O}] + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{OH}$$
Hot, concentrated, acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ gives vigorous oxidative cleavage of the double bond. Propene splits into ethanoic acid and carbon dioxide, not propanoic acid:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{hot } \text{KMnO}_4} \text{CH}_3\text{COOH} + \text{CO}_2$$

**Pick the correct row**

Only the HBr reaction correctly matches its stated product, 2-bromopropane. All other rows pair the right reagent with the wrong product.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{Br}_2\text{(aq)}$ is bromine water, not pure bromine. It adds Br and OH across the double bond to give 1-bromo-propan-2-ol, not 1-bromopropane. 1-bromopropane would require HBr with peroxide (anti-Markovnikov), not bromine water.
options.B: Incorrect. Cold, dilute, acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ is mild oxidation and forms the diol, propane-1,2-diol. It does not cleave the carbon chain to form a carboxylic acid like propanoic acid.
options.C: Correct. HBr undergoes Markovnikov electrophilic addition to propene. The H adds to C1 to give the more stable secondary carbocation on C2, then $\text{Br}^-$ attacks to give 2-bromopropane, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHBrCH}_3$.
options.D: Incorrect. Hot, concentrated, acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ cleaves the C=C bond. Propene, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$, gives ethanoic acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$) from the left fragment plus $\text{CO}_2$ from the right $\text{=CH}_2$ fragment. Propanoic acid with 3 carbons cannot form because the chain is broken.
